result.title: Two Clocks in Diffusion MLLMs: When Answers Stabilize Before Rationales Unfold
result.comment: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on BeNTo (Beyond Next-Token Prediction - Diffusion & Flow Models for Next-Generation Decoding)
result.summary: An answer candidate in a masked diffusion MLLM can stabilize while its rationale is still unfolding. We distinguish retrospective stabilization of the logged candidate from token commitment, and examine these two clocks relative to rationale generation. Analyzing our results across three visual question-answering benchmarks, we find that 89.4-98.1% of the rationale-side canvas remains unwritten at stabilization in single-block, EOS-suppressed LaViDa runs. On V*Bench, reducing block length from 128 to 8 changes this fraction from 89.4% to 1.7%, together with answer coverage and the eligible observation window. Under EOS-enabled prompting, direct instructions improve Nemotron's overall accuracy by 15.0 and 19.5 percentage points on M3CoT and ScienceQA, but reduce LaViDa/V*Bench accuracy by 11.0 points. A symmetric decomposition associates the larger absolute component of each change with coverage rather than conditional accuracy. Matched-canvas image ablations measure visual sensitivity alongside answer stabilization, separating the two temporal readouts. Together, these measurements distinguish answer stabilization, rationale unfolding, and visual sensitivity, and identify coverage as the larger component of the prompting differences.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文分析掩码扩散多模态大模型（LaViDa、Nemotron）中答案候选的“稳定”与 rationale 逐步展开的时间错位，用三个 VQA 基准测量不同 block 长度与 EOS prompting 下 rationale 画布未写比例、答案覆盖率与视觉敏感性的变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关联「THINK/STOP」的收益与成本：其答案先于 rationale 稳定、block 长度改变观测窗口等发现，可供核查 latent 推理中动态计算、停止决策与视觉证据筛选的时间结构。
